He made an entry in the record, and as far as I know, Mr. Du Toit was not a lawyer but an investigator." Your Honours, there is an entry in the documents prepared by the Viennese police concerning the approval of the magistrate, Dr. Seda, for release of items to the OTP and it is dated 20th March 1996. Your Honours will find that document in Prosecution Exhibit 104, in the English version it is page 4 of Prosecution Exhibit 104. It is a report dated 22nd April 1996, which was prepared in connection with Taubergasse 15, Door 10. This report was prepared by Bychek, Moerbauer and Panzer. It makes reference to, among other things, four allegedly seized videotapes from apartment 10. The entry in question relates to all four videotapes which I read to you now: "A copy was submitted to the UN Tribunal on 20th March 1996 after consulting the judge on duty, Dr. Seda." Nowhere in Prosecution Exhibit 104 is there any reference concerning contact with the judge regarding the release of evidence to the OTP before 20th March 1996. Your Honours, it is submitted that the cumulative effect of this evidence shows that no permission was obtained from Dr. Seda on 18th March 1996. It is further submitted that all access to the allegedly seized items by the OTP, all handling, all photocopying, Officer Moerbauer's clear recollection that documents were taken away that evening by the OTP, all of this amounts to a breach of Austrian law. I say this for this reason. It was put to Officer Panzer during his testimony and he agreed that it would be a violation of the law to allow unauthorised individuals to have access to the allegedly seized items, not to mention having those items leave police headquarters, or copies of them, because there is one point to clarify in this regard. During his testimony Officer Moerbauer said that in the case of three documents, the originals were given to an OTP officer, and taken away with him on the evening of 18th March, and during his testimony, Officer D'Hooge acknowledged that when he left police headquarters, he left police headquarters with original documents, although he says it was after 18th March. It is respectfully submitted that this is the situation at police headquarters on 18th March between 5.00 and 7.30. While documents are being examined and selected for photocopy by OTP representatives, Moerbauer is also off elsewhere in the police headquarters making photocopies. There is no record keeping taking place. There is no proof of that and, in fact, Moerbauer says there was no record keeping. No one has any idea what is being handled, moved, photocopied or taken away. Moerbauer and D'Hooge say that up to 14 people had access to room 331 that evening between 5.00 and 7.30 pm. Officer Panzer says that the OTP representatives were in the room next door, 329, with the allegedly seized items. He has these items changing rooms. Finally, Moerbauer has the documents leaving police headquarters along with the OTP representatives including in one case three original documents and there is doubt whether Dr. Seda approved of any such activities at all on 18th March 1996. Your Honours, the Prosecution's contention is that Officer Moerbauer is the central link in the chain of custody. Prosecution Exhibit 104, to which I have made reference so far, is an analysis prepared by Officer Moerbauer which was admitted into evidence, not for the truth of its contents, you will recall, but as proof that all the allegedly seized material from all three seizures was analysed methodically and consistently by Officer Moerbauer. It is submitted that not only is Prosecution Exhibit 104 completely unreliable, with Officer Moerbauer and the other Viennese police officers who have testified, the Prosecution cannot prove a single document or videotape. Would it be convenient to stop here, perhaps?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Is that your last observation or are you continuing when we have resumed?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: I will resume after the break, if that is all right, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You will.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Good afternoon, ladies and gentlemen. We hear the speed at which you are going in presenting the case has made it impossible for the interpreters to get to all other languages, so in fact, it is very likely we might not have English translation this afternoon. We might not also have the French translation, so please, will counsel appreciate that difficulty, and make sure that we have the interpretation properly. All the problem is your speed. I know you are anxious to complete what you are saying.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, thank you. I will endeavour to be aware of that fact. May I proceed?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, before the break I was attempting to review the evidence with you on the issue of the chain of custody by breaking down events into certain time periods, and we had gone from the point of seizure at both apartment 14 and INDA-Bau back to police headquarters at approximately 5.00 on the afternoon of 18th March. The second period, which we have reviewed together, relates to the evening of 18th March 1996 at police headquarters. Just before the break I was saying that the Prosecution's contention is that Officer Moerbaur is the central link in the chain of custody. Prosecution Exhibit 104 is an analysis, prepared by Officer Moerbaur, which was admitted into evidence, not for the truth of its contents, but as proof that all the allegedly seized materials from all three locations was analysed methodically and consistently by Officer Moerbaur. It is submitted that not only is Prosecution Exhibit 104 unreliable, but through Officer Moerbaur and the other Viennese police officers, it is submitted that the Prosecution cannot prove the authenticity of a single document or a single video. During his testimony, Officer Moerbaur testified that he analysed all the documents from the three alleged seizures, and that he analysed some, but not all, of the allegedly seized videos. Moerbaur analysed all the documents, he and his colleagues analysed all the videos. Officer Moerbaur testified that the videos were analysed for a period of between 10 to 15 days, beginning on 19th March 1996, so from 19th March for ten days, the videos were analysed. Moerbaur also testified that from 22nd March until 2nd April, he marked the individual documents for the first time, and he analysed them. He says this at page 3574. So the documents are marked for the first time, all the documents from all the seizures are marked -- I am sorry, from INDA-Bau and from 14 are marked for the first time by Moerbaur beginning on 22nd March and concluding on 2nd April. Let me remind your Honours of a few facts which are submitted are pertinent to this portion of my submissions. We know that none of these items were marked before leaving the premises from which they were allegedly seized. We know that none of the allegedly seized items was in a container which was marked or sealed when it left the premises. Furthermore, all these items remained unmarked when they were handled, examined, photocopied at police headquarters on 18th March 1996 from 5.00 pm until 7.30 pm. The evidence of Officer Panzer is that he marked the allegedly seized items from Door 10 at around 8.00 pm on the evening of 18th March 1996, after the OTP representatives had left that evening, and Panzer also said that he marked the alleged seized items, that is to say the videos and the folders, he claims, on 19th March, the next day. It is respectfully submitted that the chain of continuity by the time Officer Moerbaur begins his analysis of videos on 19th March, and by the time he begins his analysis of documents on 22nd March is completely non-existent, if it ever existed in the first place. It is the result of his analysis of these items during that period --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I wish I understood that conclusion. What does not exist?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: There have been so many breaks over this chain.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: That the exercise never existed or the claim to have done that never existed?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Perhaps Moerbaur did look at items, tapes and videos, but Moerbaur cannot say which ones, because they were never marked, never sealed, and they were handled by all these people at police headquarters, and photocopied. What Moerbaur looked at on the 19th with the videos, starting on 19th March, and what he may have looked at, beginning on 22nd March, he may have had something, but there is no evidence to say that that has been controlled and maintained, to know that things change. In fact from the documents we know that things did change, numbers changed, items off the Niederschrift are different when we come to his final analysis in Prosecution Exhibit 104 because by April 22nd, the documents prepared by Moerbaur and others show that different items were analysed and itemised. That is the area I want to explore with your Honours right now, through the evidence that is on the record. Just to remind your Honours that Prosecution -- this Prosecution Exhibit 104 contains all the Niederschrift and all the reports and all the evaluations, and these were the items, many of the exhibits that were shown to the Viennese police officers who testified before you, and as I said, in many of these documents, we know that allegedly seized items change as reflected in those documents. Officer Moerbaur also testified that he drew up a final report at the end of April. He testified that his final report was handed over to the judge at the regional court of Vienna at the end of April, but through his own testimony, Moerbaur does not know if the seized material was handed over to the judge at the same time as his final report. He says this at page 3580, your Honours: "Question: Was the original seized material handed over to the judge on the same day when the final report was handed over at the end of April? Answer: I do not know, because my final report with the seized items was handed over to police headquarters in Vienna, which was then subsequently transmitted to -- which then subsequently transmitted things to the court, so the headquarters addressed these documents and the seized items to the Vienna district court." Officer Moerbaur does not know if these items he analysed were handed over to the competent judge. All he can say is that the final report, along with seized items, was handed over to police headquarters in Vienna, which was then subsequently transmitted to the court in Vienna. Officer Moerbaur has doubts then about the continuity of the evidence from the time it leaves Moerbaur to the time it ends up in the district court of Vienna. For all these reasons it is submitted that Prosecution Exhibit 104 is an unreliable document. It is based on analyses of allegedly seized material by Moerbaur, and the provenance of this material is not clearly proven beyond a reasonable doubt, given all the intervening events, from the time they leave premises, to the things that happened on the evening of the 18th in police headquarters. When Moerbaur looks at these beginning on the 19th for the videos and the 22nd, for the month of March. He may have looked at things but there is no proof of what he looked at because nothing is marked, nothing arrived sealed. Your Honours, a moment ago I made the submission that the Prosecution had not proven the authenticity of a single document or video from either INDA-Bau or apartment 14. Let us review the facts. Apartment 14: no evidence was given by Unger or Winkelmann. They are the officers who allegedly conducted the search in apartment 14. We saw the inconsistent accounts given by Moerbaur and Panzer concerning the way in which the allegedly seized items from 14 returned to headquarters. Moerbaur and Panzer each claimed they had a bag. The evidence alleges, however, there was only one bag from apartment 14. We saw that together. The report of Unger and Winkelmann on 18th March is different from their Niederschrift, the same police officers prepared a Niederschrift and a first report. We go from 30 to 28 videos. The black bag has disappeared. The Prosecution is attempting to have one document allegedly seized from apartment 14 admitted into evidence. This document is identified in Prosecution Exhibit 104 as coming from a green folder, D-4. Moerbaur refers to this folder at page 3561. Your Honours may recall that during the testimony of Officer Panzer, I directed his attention to this green folder, D-4. I did it to show one thing, your Honours. As your Honours know, this Prosecution Exhibit 104 is not admitted for the truth of its contents but its proof that Officer Moerbaur had a reliable system of analysis. The Prosecution sought to have it admitted so your Honours could rely on Moerbaur's system of analysis. My intention in having Officer Panzer follow the green folder, D-4, through the Niederschrift and the records and the evaluation was to show that certain documents from the green folder, which allegedly comes from apartment 14, disappeared and appear to show up in an evaluation prepared for INDA-Bau, completely different location. I was not seeking to have Officer Panzer comment or say how that happened, I just wanted to show your Honours with one more example that Prosecution Exhibit 104 is not reliable for the purposes that the Prosecution advances it. I leave it to your Honours to review the transcript beginning on page 6630, where Officer Panzer is taken through the Niederschrift, through the report, as well as through the documents in 104, in relation to the green folder which comes from apartment --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would counsel please slow down.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Would counsel kindly slow down for the interpreters.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Yes, your Honour, thank you. I do not propose to go through that part of the transcript with your Honours, it is on page 6630. I would like to address your Honours on one aspect of the cross-examination of Mr. Panzer in relation to this green folder, D-4. I said I did not ask Officer Panzer to comment or explain why certain documents in the green folder disappeared in the final evaluation. This final evaluation being the most detailed analysis of the folder. Your Honours will recall that as we start with the Niederschrift, the record of on the premises and as we move through all of these reports and evaluations, we are going into more and more and more detailed analysis of the contents of the allegedly seized items. As I said, I did not ask Panzer to comment why certain things seemed to disappear or not mentioned in the final analysis and why they end up in an INDA-Bau evaluation, but Officer Moerbaur did offer an explanation, he did give a comment. Beginning at page 6634, Officer Panzer had this to say about the green folder D-4. He said: "I do not know what you expect me to say, because in my opinion, as far as the green folder is concerned, Moerbaur or myself brought it in, so that all these different pieces of paper could be collected in a single folder and be labelled in that way. I cannot really say any more about this green folder." Your Honours, if you look at the English version of Prosecution Exhibit 104 at page 12, you will find the final evaluation of this green folder.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Let me get this clear. Actually, what is your challenge of Exhibit 104, which is made as an aide memoire to assist in correlation of documents which were seized.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: It is admitted for those purposes. I am saying that when it was prepared by Moerbaur based on his analysis, he has no way of knowing, we have no way of knowing, through whose hands the provenance of the items he looked at because of all the intervening events that have broken the chain of custody, from the moment they were allegedly seized to the moment he gets them, beginning either 19th March in the case of the videos, or 22nd March in the case of the documents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Does that challenge go to the authenticity of the documents themselves?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Yes, because they have never been marked. We do not know whose hands they have been through, we do not know where they have been. We know that the documents show us that the quantity of items has changed. We do not know whether it is one thing, two things, different bags -- they were put in generic cardboard boxes, a generic gym bag, plastic bags, none of which are sealed, none of which are marked. In some cases, we have two gym bags from 14, we have items from INDA-Bau coming back to two officers, given to different people. We have photocopies which I submit were made in violation of the law of Austria because Judge Seda did not give his permission. We have original documents apparently leaving with an OTP investigator.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: You regard that as a fairly good speculation of what might have happened.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: It is all by juxtaposing the testimony of the witnesses they have confirmed it. Why are there problems with the documents? Their testimony is bringing out the problems, your Honour, that is my submission. We are getting conflicting versions on some pretty fundamental aspects of care and control and continuity. There must be a reason why the numbers changed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: It is your submission, I think you can go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Return to the green folder, D-4, Officer Panzer says that he and Moerbaur brought it in. They are the ones who created the green folder. To return to Exhibit 104 at page 12 of the English version, you will see that across the top of that document at page 12 in capital letters we have the word evaluation, followed by this: "Evaluation of the green folder entitled mail which was seized in the flat of Zejnil Delalic in Vienna, 17 Taubergasse 15/14." That is the heading of the evaluation. Officer Panzer says he and Moerbaur created this file to put different pieces of paper in. That is the testimony I just read to you. In the evaluation of the green folder, the green folder is represented at "mail", the correspondence, a correspondence folder which is seized in apartment 14; in other words this green folder is not represented as a folder which he and Moerbaur brought in to put different pieces of paper in, it is represented as a folder with the word "mail" on it, coming from apartment 14. In my respectful submission, this is an attempt -- in an attempt to explain to counsel why things have disappeared from the green folder, Officer Panzer has admitted to having created a folder putting the name "mail" on it. It is submitted this is admitted fabrication of this green folder and it is consistent with Officer Panzer, his admission to my learned colleague Mr. Moran at page 6662 where he agreed with Mr. Moran that he was trying to mislead a judge into thinking that Officer Moerbaur had signed the arrest report, when in fact Officer Panzer had forged Moerbaur's signature. That arrest report is D67/1. Allow me to sum up on apartment 14. It is respectfully submitted that the Prosecution has not proven or authenticated the items allegedly seized from apartment 14. No evidence was heard from the officer who allegedly conducted the search. There is conflicting testimony as between Moerbaur and Panzer over care and control of the bag, they have two bags and the documents say there was one. There are the events which transpired on the evening of 18th March 1996 at police headquarters which affects the continuity once again. Finally, it is my submission that this proof of fabrication involving evidence in apartment 14, the green folder. It is further submitted that the Prosecution has failed to prove a single document or video from INDA-Bau. Your Honours heard the testimony of Officer Navrat, who collected the allegedly seized items from INDA-Bau. He testified, Officer Panzer testified, that he did not mark a single item among the seized material before leaving the premises at INDA-Bau. Before your Honours he did not identify, nor was he asked to identify, any videos allegedly confiscated during that search. Your Honours, the fact of the matter is this: that in order to save himself and the Prosecution a lot of embarrassment, Officer Navrat could not be shown the videos. The Prosecution would have to have put 54 videos in front of Navrat and ask him to choose the 51 he said he seized according to his Niederschrift and report. Officer Navrat was, however, shown 12 folders, which he allegedly confiscated from INDA-Bau, which he had testified to not having marked before leaving. Before your Honours Mr. Niemann showed 12 folders to Officer Navrat, and beginning at page 5649 of the transcript we have this exchange between Mr. Niemann and Mr. Navrat. Mr. Niemann asked the question: "Mr. Navrat, would you please look at these documents that you have just been shown, go through them one by one and I will ask you some questions about them. You do not need to open them at this stage if you can tell me what they are just by looking at the outside. Could you tell me what they are? Do you recognise what those documents are? Answer: I take it that these 12 folders are those I provisionally seized. Question: In order to satisfy yourself that they are the documents that you seized, would you care to inspect them in greater detail? You may look inside if that assists you. Answer: I think it might be helpful for me to have a closer look, if I could have a closer look, that might help. Question: Please have a closer look. While you are doing that, if it is at all possible to do both the tasks together, could you attempt to sort them in the same order as you set them out in the record of the search document, the Niederschrift, Exhibit 136, which I think is before you -- 165, sorry." Then there is a pause. Your Honours will recall Navrat opened a folder or two, looked in at a document or two and made three piles. Mr. Niemann continues: "Now that you have had a chance to look at them, do you recognise those documents, Mr. Navrat. Answer: Yes, I do recognise them. I have striven to break them down according to what I put in the search record. Question: I think you have set them out in three piles on the desk, is that right, in front of you? Answer: Yes, that is right. Question: I take it is the large pile the one relating to the 8? Answer: Yes, that is right, yes. Question: Which one relates to the two Mucic documents? Can you just point to it with your fingers? Answer: These to my right (indicates). Question: And the other two, are those two which are referred to as containing newspaper articles? Answer: Yes." Your Honour, with all due respect, Officer Navrat never put an identification mark on the folders he allegedly seized at INDA-Bau. Before you he put 12 generic coloured folders in three piles of 8, 2 and 2, according to what he said was in the Niederschrift. The best Officer Navrat could say about the folders is: "I take it that these are the folders. I have striven to break them down." The only thing Officer Navrat did not say, but one got the impression he wanted to say after making the three piles was "did I do it right?" Your Honours, it is submitted that this exercise with Officer Navrat and the 12 folders proved absolutely nothing. The first link of the chain for INDA-Bau is never proven. The next attempt your Honours saw at proving the folders allegedly seized at INDA-Bau was through Panzer. His testimony was to the effect that he put stickers on the previously unmarked folders on 19th March 1996. This is the day after events at police headquarters in Vienna on the evening of 18th March, as I pointed out earlier, where the unmarked folders were examined, opened and photocopied. In relation to these folders and the markings of officer -- that Officer Panzer claims he put on them, I direct your Honours to the Bericht prepared in connection with INDA-Bau, dated 22nd April 1996. This report is Prosecution -- is in Prosecution Exhibit 104, at page 15 of the English version. It is a short one page document. In this report, folders are identified as I/1 to I/12 and the videos are identified as I/13 to I/66. What is of interest, and I will read this to you, is the last paragraph of this report of April 22nd 19967: "The objects secured have been stored in a cardboard box. I is the first letter of the name of the individual involved. The numbers allow for checking against the inventory. Stickers have been put on some of the objects." Your Honour, this document, dated 22nd April 1996 states that stickers have been put on some of the objects, which means obviously the stickers have not been put on all of the objects from INDA-Bau, as Officer Panzer said he did on 19th March 1996 and this report I am quoting from is signed by Panzer. It is submitted that on the basis of this report from April 22nd, there is reasonable doubt as to whether Officer Panzer placed stickers on the allegedly seized items from INDA-Bau on 19th March, as he said he did during his testimony, or perhaps the stickers Officer Panzer affixed on 19th March have been removed, or perhaps this record makes reference to folders without stickers which are different from the ones that he did put stickers on on 19th March. The folders, not their contents, were admitted into evidence on the basis of Panzer's testimony. It is submitted that this entry in this report of April 22nd raises a doubt as to whether the 12 folders were marked on the 19th as Officer Panzer says they were. Finally, your Honours, in regards to all the documents from 14 and INDA-Bau, I deal with them together to make this point. There is further testimony given before you by Officer Moerbaur which it is submitted is determinative in showing that the chain of custody cannot be established. After all the breaks in the chain of custody which we submit have already been established, there was one more which your Honours should consider. Officer Moerbaur testified that he put his sticker on each individual document that he analysed between 22nd March and 2nd April 1996; in other words the contents of these folders, not the exterior. This is the only evidence before your Honours that the documents were marked or identified. When, however, Officer Moerbaur testified before this Tribunal, and was shown Prosecution Exhibits 104 to 147, those are the two binders, he could only see his mark on one document. Officer Moerbaur's explanation was that someone must have removed his mark from all but one of the documents which are Exhibits 104 to 147. In fact, it was your Honour Judge Karibi-Whyte who put this question to Moerbaur at page 3755, line 22. Your Honour asked: "Now, is it your evidence that initially you put marks on them but these marks were subsequently removed? Answer: The markings have been removed, that is right."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could you please slow down a bit?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: I will slow down, thank you. Further on this point at page 3756, line 25, the question was put point blank to Moerbaur by my learned colleague Madam Residovic: "Question: Mr. Moerbaur, in addition to the fact that your marks do not exist on the documents, is it also true that there is no mark on any of the documents shown to you during the hearing showing where that document comes from? Answer: The individual documents had, except for this exception. They did not have any of my references, so none of the documents had my references." To sum up, your Honours, it is respectfully submitted that the Prosecution has not proven the authenticity of the material seized from INDA-Bau. Videos were not and could not be shown to Officer Navrat, the officer who allegedly seized them from the premises. Furthermore, it is respectfully submitted that the Prosecution has not proven the documents allegedly seized from INDA-Bau, neither Navrat nor Panzer, in our submission, have identified the 12 folders beyond a reasonable doubt. Navrat cannot identify the folders at all, your Honours. He never marked the ones that he claims that he confiscated at INDA-Bau, and his demonstration before you making three piles proved nothing. The report prepared by Panzer on 22nd April 1996 stating that stickers had not been put on some items from INDA-Bau conflicts with his testimony that he had marked everything allegedly seized from INDA-Bau on 19th March. And Moerbaur, the only person who claims to have actually marked the individual documents from INDA-Bau, testified in this court that the marks he says he put on the documents were no longer there. Furthermore, Moerbaur says he put his marks on the INDA-Bau documents between 22nd March and 2nd April, that is six days after the events which transpired on the evening of 18th March 1996 at police headquarters, involving all these items. The cumulative effect, your Honours, of all this testimony clearly demonstrates, in our submission, that the chain of custody has been -- chain of custody regarding these documents has been broken several times over and the Prosecution has not proved the reliability of these items from INDA-Bau. Your Honours, that concludes my submissions on the facts. I do have some submissions to make on the law and with your indulgence, perhaps we only have 25 minutes, I could do that tomorrow morning, it may be more appropriate. I do not think I will finish by 5.30.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: We still have sufficient time for you to conclude the arguments.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: Your Honours, at the outset of my submissions I stated that the defendant Delalic relies on two bases for requesting that this Tribunal suppress the allegedly seized items from apartment 14 and INDA-Bau, first on the basis of the two preliminary motions filed pursuant to sub-rule 73 and second, on the basis of an objection based on Article 20(1) of the statute, the fair trial provision, and Article 21(3) of the statute, the right of the accused to be presumed innocent, as well as rules 89(B) and Rule 95 of the rules. We have heard submissions earlier today on both these rules, but for completeness and with your indulgence I would like to read in full both rules 89 and 95.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Do you really have to read those rules? They are very well known.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: All right. Specifically then in regard to Rule 95, it is submitted that the evidence in this matter shows that an illegal search and seizure occurred which violates the basic human right to the right to privacy. This right is enshrined in the international human rights treaties, and I make reference to three such instruments to guide your Honours. First Article 17 of the international covenant on civil and political rights from 1966, an international convention of the UN which has been ratified by Austria. Second, Article 8, paragraph 2 of the European Convention on human rights of 1950, which has been ratified by Austria. Third, Article 11 of the American Convention on Human Rights 1969. By way of example I would like to quote and read into the record Article 8 of the European Convention on human rights. Article 8, paragraph 1 states: "Everyone has the right to respect for his private and family life, his home and his correspondence." Paragraph 2 of Article 8 says: "There shall be no interference by a public authority with the exercise of his right, except such as in accordance with the law and is necessary in a democratic society in the interests of national security, public safety, or the economic well being of the country for the prevention of disorder or crime for the protection of health or morals or for the protection of the rights and freedoms of others." The right to privacy is subject therefore to interference by a public authority in accordance with the law. It is respectfully submitted that the breaches of the Austrian law in this matter amount to an illegal search and seizure having been conducted. It is submitted that the breaches of the Austrian code are as follows. I go back to Article 139 and the search warrant. The evidence shows that there was no link between Zejnil Delalic and apartment 14 and INDA-Bau. There may be no question that Judge Seda issued the search warrant; the question is, on what information given to him by the authorities, and particularly Gschwendt, did he base his issuance of the search warrant? Zejnil Delalic was living in Munich Germany, where he was arrested on 18th March. If I can just open a parentheses for a moment by way of explanation, it may be appropriate to point out to your Honours when looking at the documentation filed in connection with the Rule 73 preliminary motion that there is reference both to seizures in Vienna and Munich. I raise this so your Honours understand why both Munich and Vienna are in those motions, so there is no confusion on your part. Mr. Delalic was living in Munich and, as you know, he was arrested there and there were seizures conducted in Munich and over 1700 pages of documents were seized from him in Munich. At this point in our argument on the question of admissibility, there is no need to make specific submissions concerning Munich. However, should we go beyond the issue of suppression, your Honours may hear more about the relationship between the Munich documents and the Vienna documents. At this point, I limit my submissions to violations based on the issuance of the search warrant. The second article referred to was Article 142(2), having Sanda Mucic, a 14 year old girl, witness the search, and the third article is Article 145, paragraph 3. I have not mentioned this article so far in my submissions, but you will recall that it was read to Officer Navrat at page 6591. I will read only the first sentence of this provision to you now, as I submit it is the most relevant. The first sentence of this section says: "The documents which are to be used in judicial proceedings and which cannot be properly recorded shall be put in an envelope and sealed with an official seal." The remainder of this paragraph describes that both the police and the property owner may affix his or her seal and it also provides for procedures on how and when the seal may be broken. Officer Panzer acknowledged that he was aware of Article 145, paragraph 3, and that members of his police in Vienna are made aware of this article through their training. This provision was apparently ignored by the police in Vienna on 18th March 1996. Your Honours, the legislator in Austria, in his wisdom, chose to put these articles that I have just referred to in the Austrian code of criminal procedure. It is submitted that they were included in the code to protect the right to privacy. They are there to provide protection to citizens against unwarranted intrusions by the authorities into their private lives, which brings Austria in line with its international obligations under international human rights law. It is submitted that these are also part of Austrian law, out of a concern for obtaining and using evidence in judicial proceedings, like this one. These procedures are there so that courts can have confidence in the work that the police does in conducting a search and seizure. So the courts can have confidence ultimately that if evidence adduced at trial is admitted, the court can rely on it to determine guilt or innocence while ensuring a fair trial and the presumption of innocence and other fundamental principles which underpin a criminal trial. When these procedures are not followed, as it was in our case, no one can have confidence in the evidence the Prosecution is trying to have admitted. But it is submitted that the illegalities go beyond breaches of these three articles of the Austrian code of criminal procedure. Not being able to establish the chain of custody constitutes a fatal flaw in procedures which may be seen, as well as a serious breach of the protection that a person is entitled to under human rights law. It is the same when police officers admit to forging documents with the intention of misleading a judge, as Officer Panzer admitted to. It is the same in regards to the conduct of the investigator of the OTP, Sabina Manke, in this matter. Sabina Manke was a potential witness in this case because she transported the allegedly seized material from the court in Vienna to The Hague knowing that she could be called as a witness. She followed proceedings in the public gallery until spotted by Defence counsel. Thereafter she was seen over the noon hour one day by Defence counsel with Officer Navrat while he was on a break during his giving of testimony. Sabina Manke failed to indicate to Mr. Niemann, who was investigating this matter, that she had already been a witness in this trial, for when he reported back to the Tribunal he was unaware that she had given testimony. In fairness to Mr. Niemann, who joined this trial in mid July and who is involved in other cases, it was incumbent on Sabina Manke to tell him that. Your Honours also know that when Sabina Manke was a witness in this trial on 8th May, she was found to have written incorrect, highly prejudicial information about Mr. Delalic in internal documents prepared by her for her superiors. The documents in which this inaccurate and damaging information contained were prepared by Ms. Manke in the same month of March 1996.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Is this part of your argument about the validity of the warrants?

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: No, your Honour, it is the conduct of Ms. Manke, like that of Officer Panzer, reflects impropriety and bad faith.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I thought you were arguing the illegality of the warrants.

utterances.speaker: MR. O'SULLIVAN
utterances.text: I am arguing the full context, your Honour. It casts doubt and suspicion on the motives of the people who were involved. Your Honour, this is why the law, and in particular our statute, our rules, have international human rights safeguards built into it. That is why the legal standards are set at beyond reasonable doubt. In this regard and with all due respect to Mr. Niemann, I must strongly disagree with some of his views regarding the way procedures were carried out by police in Vienna. In the record, Mr. Niemann has said this about police procedures on page 3763. In regard to police procedures: "There was regularity in the procedures that were followed and that the police in Vienna had gone according to law in the methods in which they sought to seize these documents. There may be arguments that the letter of the law was not complied with in every particular aspect, but it is certainly evidence of the fact that procedures were followed according to law." Mr. Niemann also said this about Mr. Moerbaur and the allegedly confiscated material: "Moerbaur cannot talk about whether he knew where precisely they came from, but he was able to give some evidence of the provenance of these documents and his ability to identify them." Your Honour, it is my respectful submission that before this International Criminal Tribunal, such standards fall far short of what this institution is intended to accomplish, particularly in the context of this matter, where the OTP has collaborated with an elite division of the Vienna police, whose duties include national security and state protection. Let us not forget that the problems associated with search and seizure that I have been highlighting were caused by Austrian police officers with 15, 18, 20 years experience. In this context, it is submitted that such police officers by their own conduct have violated the protections that are guaranteed to individuals under international human rights law. We have heard said in this courtroom that we are not bound by national rules of law, but if as it is submitted here, criminal procedure of Austria has been violated, such violations cannot be ignored when they are scrutinised by this Tribunal. Allow me to respond to one point made this morning by Mr. Niemann before finishing, when he referred generally to admissibility of documents. He referred to a Nuremberg trial, Krupp. There he said the court admitted seized documents from the office of the accused with no proof of provenance. I make three comments. In our case, the Prosecution has not proven that there is a link between Mr. Delalic and apartment 14 and INDA-Bau. Second, the Prosecution has not proven that the allegedly seized items came from apartment 14 and INDA-Bau. The Nuremberg court did not have Rule 95, like this Tribunal does, which directs the Tribunal to turn to internationally protected human rights which have become a part of the international law since Nuremberg. Your Honours, I have addressed you at length on this matter, at great length perhaps. Even though the Prosecutor has the burden of proof, I feel I had to explain it to you in detail. There is a lot of evidence over a very long period with frequent interruptions. All I have left to say is that I respectfully request this Tribunal to suppress all the allegedly seized items from Taubergasse 15, Door 14 and from INDA-Bau which the Prosecution wishes to tender, for I submit that this is illegally obtained, unauthenticated unreliable evidence. Should, however, your Honours decide not to suppress this evidence, the Defence, Mr. Delalic reserves the right to object at the appropriate time to each and every piece of evidence on the basis of hearsay, reliability, relevance and probative value. I thank you for your attention, your Honours. That concludes my submissions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Thank you very much for your argument. Actually, I thought it would not be right if I do not mention that as interesting as your arguments have been, forensic presentation of arguments are more decent and tidier when they do not give offence. I do not see any reason for referring to persons, who perhaps their conduct need not be referred to for the purposes of this argument. I leave it at that, but frankly, my understanding of your argument is that you use your words carefully, and not make undue reference which would give offence. I think we are almost at the end of the day, but I think you might be allowed to start now.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: I can start now if your Honours like.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: Yes, and continue tomorrow morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Your Honours, in the submissions of Mr. O'Sullivan he placed a great deal of reliance in terms of having the evidence suppressed on what he termed broadly, I think, as illegality, illegality in perhaps the warrant itself and then illegality in the procedures that were followed. I think in all jurisdictions it is true to say that illegally obtained evidence, even if it is shown to be illegally obtained, is not automatically excluded. In many jurisdictions, illegally obtained evidence can be admitted at discretion, and in some jurisdictions with perhaps constitutional provisions, there generally is a good faith rule that can be applied by the court, but by and large, your Honours, the principle that illegally obtained evidence can be excluded is based on the fact of an examination of what it is that happened and the extent of the illegality. One of the principal factors that a court looks to in a national jurisdiction in terms of illegality is the conduct of the police in what they did. Your Honours, the courts cannot join with the police in all instances in condoning a total disregard of the law, an illegality. Courts cannot be seen to be part of that. The courts uphold and enforce the law. When police officers disregard the law, the courts must do what they can to try and rectify the situation, to try and prevent it from happening again, to the extent of their power. One of the most salient sanctions available to a court to control improper behaviour by a police officer is to exclude the evidence. The rationale is that police officers will hopefully ultimately desist from illegal conduct if they can see that the fruits of that illegal conduct render their efforts worthless, because when they come to the court to produce the evidence which they have obtained in total disregard of the law, courts reject it and will not accept it. But, your Honours, can this Tribunal seriously hope to discipline Austrian police? I mean, let us call it country X. Let us not relate to a particular country. There are some countries, your Honours, could not care less whether your Honours admitted the evidence or not. They could not care. They co-operate to the extent that they feel it is necessary, or they do not co-operate at all, and if your Honours do not admit the evidence they do not care, so if one of the principal objectives of excluding illegally obtained evidence is to discipline the police, that has a very important function in a national setting where the courts are there to supervise the administration of the law and particularly the behaviour of law enforcement officers when they come before it. But in my submission, that principle has no relevance here whatsoever. That does not mean to say, your Honours, that you should disregard entirely that. We have all seen from time to time attempts in various places around the world to extract evidence by not so much just technically illegal means, but by means of torture, by means of false imprisonment, incarceration, by means of starvation, by means of subjecting the person to the point where they either give up things or say things which suits the people that wish to obtain that material or evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: If I might draw attention to the real focus of these arguments, if my memory serves me right, I think the main contention is that the warrant which was executed on these premises was illegally obtained.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: The warrant in the first place, your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: The warrant itself. Secondly, that perhaps the procedure adopted in the execution of the warrant and the obtaining of the evidence, the documents and the like, did not comply with the procedure in Austria, and also the chain of possession of the property which was discovered in these premises has not been complied with.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Those issues are tied up with the illegality question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: May I add, if the evidence is not admissible --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: If the evidence is not admissible in an Austrian court because of irregularity in carrying out a search, would it be proper for this Tribunal to accept that evidence?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: It may or may not be, your Honours. I would put it the other way round. In my submission, this evidence is admissible in Austria and --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: Despite not falling within the provision.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE JAN
utterances.text: That is why I asked Mr. O'Sullivan whether there are any cases from the Austrian jurisdiction pursuing this particular provision.

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: What I have been informed, your Honour -- I hasten to inform the court that I am no expert in Austrian law, but what I have been told is that this evidence would be admissible and the reason why it is admissible is that it is done under the supervision of the judge, the supervising judge, in this case Judge Seda. The judge who is an investigating judge, would take the material himself and make determinations on it according to how it is that he is to frame the case. I am instructed that under those circumstances irregularities of this kind would not affect the admissibility of the documents, should the judge determine to use them.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: We will continue tomorrow morning with this argument. We will know actually our bearing.

utterances.speaker: MR. GREAVES
utterances.text: Could I just interrupt and I hope it is not out of order to do so. My learned friend has just given us what he has been told about Austrian law. Perhaps he might like to think overnight about this point: would the judge have admitted the evidence if he knew that he had been misled by Gschwendt as to the existence or not of facts supporting the suspicion justifying the warrant. If the judge has been misled by the police officers as to existence of facts, would the evidence still be admissible in those circumstances?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: These are matters for consideration --

utterances.speaker: MR. ACKERMAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, may I request that Mr. Landzo be excused from appearance tomorrow? He has a medical appointment, I think at 11.00 or 12.00 tomorrow. There is nothing going on here tomorrow that is of any interest to him. None of us object to that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I think he can be excused for purely legal argument.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, if I can make the same request for Mr. Delic so he can rest his back for another day.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KARIBI-WHYTE
utterances.text: I think they can stay away as long as they are not involved in any disputation here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MORAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, on behalf of Mr. Delic, thank you very much.

procedural_notes.text: (Court adjourned until 10.00 am the following day)
